title: Concepts of happiness
paragraphs: How are you feeling today? Our emotions can vary considerably depending on many factors, including our health, wealth, relationships and where we live. But sometimes we need to take a step back and think about what happiness really means and how we can find it.

Maybe we should take a leaf out of Finland's book – last year the UN's World Happiness Report found the country to be the happiest place on Earth. The report looked at 'subjective well-being'. That's how happy people feel they are and why - based on factors such as, economic strength, social support, life expectancy, freedom of choice, generosity, and perceived corruption.

This is just one way of measuring happiness. Research has also suggested that while personal feelings of pleasure are the accepted definition of happiness in Western cultures, East Asian cultures tend to see happiness as social harmony, and in some parts of Africa and India it's more about shared experiences and family.

Author and journalist Helen Russell has been looking at the positive characteristics of a country's population to see what makes them happy and found Japan to be one of the most content. She told the BBC that this was due to their concept of wabi-sabi – "this traditional Japanese concept around celebrating imperfection… it's this idea that there is a beauty in ageing, it's to be celebrated rather than trying to disguise it." So, basically, we should be happy with who we are and rejoice in our faults and individuality. That's something to put a smile on our faces!

But if you're feeling down in the dumps because your home country doesn't have a happiness concept to follow, consider some self-help ideas that the BBC programme Hacking Happiness has been looking into. These include being virtuous, finding something to be passionate about, enjoying the here and now and being altruistic – helping others.

However, our pursuit of happiness could make us miserable as we try to meet society’s expectations and goals, making us anxious and stressed. Also, having too little experience of negative emotions can make us less adept at facing new challenges.

vocabulary.entry: vary considerably /ˈveəri kənˈsɪdərəbli/ 发生很大变化；差异显著
vocabulary.example: Temperatures vary considerably between day and night in the desert.
vocabulary.translation: 沙漠地区昼夜温差很大。

vocabulary.entry: take a step back /teɪk ə step bæk/ 退一步；暂缓行动
vocabulary.example: We need to take a step back and evaluate the situation objectively.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要退一步，客观评估当前形势。

vocabulary.term: take a leaf out of one's book
vocabulary.entry: take a leaf out of one's book /teɪk ə liːf aʊt ɒv wʌnz bʊk/ 效仿某人；以某人为榜样
vocabulary.example: We should take a leaf out of her book and start recycling more.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该效仿她，开始更多地进行回收利用。

vocabulary.entry: subjective well-being /səbˈdʒektɪv ˈwel biːɪŋ/ 主观幸福感
vocabulary.example: Subjective well-being is an important indicator of people's quality of life.
vocabulary.translation: 主观幸福感是衡量人们生活质量的重要指标。

vocabulary.entry: life expectancy /laɪf ɪkˈspektənsi/ 预期寿命
vocabulary.example: Improved medical care has increased life expectancy in many countries.
vocabulary.translation: 医疗水平的提升提高了许多国家的人口预期寿命。

vocabulary.entry: perceived corruption /pəˈsiːvd kəˈrʌpʃn/ 对腐败的感知
vocabulary.example: The survey includes questions about perceived corruption in the local government.
vocabulary.translation: 这项调查包含关于民众对地方政府腐败感知的问题。

vocabulary.entry: social harmony /ˈsəʊʃl ˈhɑːməni/ 社会和谐
vocabulary.example: Social harmony is essential for the stable development of a country.
vocabulary.translation: 社会和谐对于一个国家的稳定发展至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: shared experiences /ʃeəd ɪkˈspɪəriənsɪz/ 共享的经历（复数）
vocabulary.example: Shared experiences strengthen the bond between family members.
vocabulary.translation: 共同的经历会加深家庭成员之间的联系。

vocabulary.entry: wabi-sabi /ˈwɑːbi ˈsɑːbi/ 侘寂（日本传统美学理念，崇尚缺憾之美）
vocabulary.example: Wabi-sabi emphasizes the beauty of imperfection and transience.
vocabulary.translation: 侘寂美学强调缺憾与转瞬即逝之美。

vocabulary.entry: disguise /dɪsˈɡaɪz/ v. 掩饰；伪装
vocabulary.example: She tried to disguise her disappointment with a smile.
vocabulary.translation: 她试图用微笑掩饰自己的失望。

vocabulary.entry: rejoice in /rɪˈdʒɔɪs ɪn/ 欣然接受；为……感到高兴
vocabulary.example: She rejoices in her unique personality instead of following others.
vocabulary.translation: 她欣然接受自己独特的性格，而不是盲从他人。

vocabulary.entry: individuality /ˌɪndɪˌvɪdʒuˈæləti/ n. 个性；独特性
vocabulary.example: The school encourages students to develop their individuality.
vocabulary.translation: 这所学校鼓励学生发展自己的个性。

vocabulary.entry: down in the dumps /daʊn ɪn ðə dʌmps/ 情绪低落；闷闷不乐
vocabulary.example: He's been down in the dumps since he failed the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 自从考试失利后，他就一直闷闷不乐。

vocabulary.entry: self-help ideas /self help aɪˈdɪəz/ 自助方法；自我提升的建议（复数）
vocabulary.example: This book is full of practical self-help ideas for dealing with stress.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书里满是应对压力的实用自助方法。

vocabulary.entry: virtuous /ˈvɜːtʃuəs/ adj. 有美德的；品行端正的
vocabulary.example: She is a virtuous person who always helps those in need.
vocabulary.translation: 她是个品行端正的人，总是帮助有困难的人。

vocabulary.entry: be passionate about /bi ˈpæʃənət əˈbaʊt/ 对……充满热情
vocabulary.example: He is passionate about playing the piano and practices every day.
vocabulary.translation: 他对弹钢琴充满热情，每天都坚持练习。

vocabulary.entry: the here and now /ðə hɪə ənd naʊ/ 当下；此时此刻
vocabulary.example: Instead of worrying about the future, we should enjoy the here and now.
vocabulary.translation: 与其为未来担忧，不如享受当下的时光。

vocabulary.entry: altruistic /ˌæltruˈɪstɪk/ adj. 利他的；无私的
vocabulary.example: His altruistic behavior has won the respect of everyone around him.
vocabulary.translation: 他无私的行为赢得了周围所有人的尊重。

vocabulary.entry: pursuit of /pəˈsjuːt ɒv/ 对……的追求
vocabulary.example: Her pursuit of perfection sometimes makes her overly critical.
vocabulary.translation: 她对完美的追求有时会让她过于挑剔。

vocabulary.entry: meet one's expectations /miːt wʌnz ˌekspekˈteɪʃnz/ 达到某人的期望（复数）
vocabulary.example: The new product failed to meet customers' expectations.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新产品没能达到消费者的期望。

vocabulary.entry: adept at /əˈdept æt/ 擅长；熟练于
vocabulary.example: She is adept at solving complex problems quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 她擅长快速解决复杂的问题。

vocabulary.entry: negative emotions /ˈneɡətɪv ɪˈməʊʃnz/ 负面情绪（复数）
vocabulary.example: Learning to manage negative emotions is an important life skill.
vocabulary.translation: 学会管理负面情绪是一项重要的生活技能。

sentences.english: Our emotions can vary considerably depending on many factors, including our health, wealth, relationships and where we live.
sentences.chinese: 我们的情绪会因诸多因素而发生很大变化，包括健康状况、经济条件、人际关系以及居住环境。

sentences.english: But sometimes we need to take a step back and think about what happiness really means and how we can find it.
sentences.chinese: 但有时我们需要退一步思考，幸福到底意味着什么，以及我们该如何找到它。

sentences.english: Maybe we should take a leaf out of Finland's book – last year the UN's World Happiness Report found the country to be the happiest place on Earth.
sentences.chinese: 或许我们应该借鉴芬兰的做法——去年联合国《世界幸福报告》将这个国家评为全球最幸福的地方。

sentences.english: The report looked at 'subjective well-being'. That's how happy people feel they are and why - based on factors such as, economic strength, social support, life expectancy, freedom of choice, generosity, and perceived corruption.
sentences.chinese: 该报告关注的是“主观幸福感”，也就是人们自我感知的幸福程度及其背后的原因，其衡量依据包括经济实力、社会支持、预期寿命、选择自由、慷慨程度以及对腐败的感知等因素。

sentences.english: This is just one way of measuring happiness.
sentences.chinese: 这只是衡量幸福的一种方式。

sentences.english: Research has also suggested that while personal feelings of pleasure are the accepted definition of happiness in Western cultures, East Asian cultures tend to see happiness as social harmony, and in some parts of Africa and India it's more about shared experiences and family.
sentences.chinese: 研究还表明，虽然西方文化将个人愉悦感视为幸福的公认定义，但东亚文化更倾向于将幸福看作社会和谐，而在非洲和印度的一些地区，幸福则更多与共享的经历和家庭相关。

sentences.english: Author and journalist Helen Russell has been looking at the positive characteristics of a country's population to see what makes them happy and found Japan to be one of the most content.
sentences.chinese: 作家兼记者海伦·拉塞尔一直致力于研究一个国家民众的积极特质，探寻他们幸福的根源，她发现日本是幸福感最高的国家之一。

sentences.english: She told the BBC that this was due to their concept of wabi-sabi – "this traditional Japanese concept around celebrating imperfection… it's this idea that there is a beauty in ageing, it's to be celebrated rather than trying to disguise it."
sentences.chinese: 她在接受BBC采访时表示，这源于日本人的“侘寂”理念——“这是一种崇尚缺憾之美的日本传统理念……这种理念认为衰老之中自有美感，衰老值得庆祝，而非刻意掩饰。”

sentences.english: So, basically, we should be happy with who we are and rejoice in our faults and individuality.
sentences.chinese: 所以，从根本上来说，我们应该欣然接纳自己，为自身的缺点和独特之处感到欣喜。

sentences.english: That's something to put a smile on our faces!
sentences.chinese: 这足以让我们展露笑颜！

sentences.english: But if you're feeling down in the dumps because your home country doesn't have a happiness concept to follow, consider some self-help ideas that the BBC programme Hacking Happiness has been looking into.
sentences.chinese: 但如果你因为自己的国家没有可供效仿的幸福理念而感到闷闷不乐，不妨参考一下BBC节目《破解幸福密码》中探讨的一些自助方法。

sentences.english: These include being virtuous, finding something to be passionate about, enjoying the here and now and being altruistic – helping others.
sentences.chinese: 这些方法包括坚守美德、找到自己热爱的事物、活在当下以及践行利他主义——也就是帮助他人。

sentences.english: However, our pursuit of happiness could make us miserable as we try to meet society’s expectations and goals, making us anxious and stressed.
sentences.chinese: 然而，当我们为了迎合社会的期望和目标而追逐幸福时，反而可能会陷入痛苦，变得焦虑不堪、压力重重。

sentences.english: Also, having too little experience of negative emotions can make us less adept at facing new challenges.
sentences.chinese: 此外，若体验负面情绪的经历过少，我们应对新挑战的能力也会随之变弱。
